summary: Patch replaces the DATA-first deletion in SSTable.delete(Descriptor, Set<Component>) with an ascending last-modified sort, then deletes every component through FileUtils.delete(String). Applied the logic.md and boundary.md checklists (categories were empty). Read the full diff (small tier) and the code it touches: FileUtils.delete(String) and deleteWithConfirm, discoverComponentsFor, LogTransaction's SSTableTidier path, and LogFile.verifyRecord. Not reviewed: nothing.

findings.rule: logic: control flow and error handling (failure swallowed, wrong return value)
findings.problem: Before this patch, DATA and every non-SUMMARY component were removed with FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError on failure. The tidier catches that, adds the task to failedDeletions and retries after GC or on restart. The patch routes all components through FileUtils.delete(String), which returns f.delete() as a boolean and discards it. Trigger: a component cannot be unlinked (EACCES, EBUSY on Windows, read-only mount). The loop continues, SSTable.delete returns true, and the tidier treats the sstable as fully deleted. The leftover files are never retried, and the transaction log is cleaned up on the false belief that deletion succeeded.
findings.fix: Keep the confirming delete for the sorted loop, e.g. FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) in place of FileUtils.delete(...), so a failed unlink propagates as before. Keep the non-confirming delete only for SUMMARY if that asymmetry was intentional.

findings.rule: logic: ordering invariant not enforced on the path the ticket describes
findings.problem: The ticket's scenario runs through SSTableTidier. That path still calls delete(datafile) on Data.db at line 396 before SSTable.delete at line 401, so DATA is always removed first regardless of timestamp. The patch only sorts inside SSTable.delete. Trigger: Data.db is the most recently modified component when the REMOVE record is written (its mtime is the record's updateTime). The tidier deletes it first, the max mtime drops, and a crash midway through leaves a REMOVE record whose timestamp no longer matches disk. On restart LogFile.verifyRecord flags it as corrupt and the node does not start, which is the failure the ticket describes.
findings.fix: Drop the explicit delete(datafile) at lines 393-396 and let SSTable.delete handle DATA in timestamp order (or pass the DATA-exists check through the sorted loop). Then add a LogTransaction test where Data.db has the newest mtime.
